conrepair.distribution: Author's CAV 2014 JAR, 47,917,114 bytes. Prebuilt release tested; no source rebuild.
conrepair.language_and_defect: Restricted C; synchronization/atomic sections and instruction ordering for concurrent assertions.
conrepair.input: Its own C dialect identifies thread functions by name and uses lock(int)/unlock(int). The implementation runs its bundled CBMC/Z3 and consumes its textual output. No documented input option for a Deagle JSON trace.

runs.reason: CPAchecker parser stops at pthread_mutex_t, line 5.
CPAchecker parser rejects CASTExpressionList at the glibc assert expansion in the preprocessed translation unit.

conrepair.adaptation: Would require a separate front end or validated translation of the thread lifecycle, mutex, joins, target assertion and source locations, then mapping its changes back to program.c.

liss.binary: No executable in the inspected authors' tree or published GitHub releases. Local build did not produce liss.
liss.language_and_defect: Restricted C; synthesizes locks by comparing preemptive and non-preemptive trace languages.
liss.input: Custom langinc.h primitives and simultaneous thread starts; pthread synchronization is ignored. The program internally generates automaton traces.
liss.build: After fetching both pinned sources from codeload and installing Boost 1.74, module-mode configure found Boost but could not find LLVM (3.6 requested). Jammy lacked libclang-3.6-dev and llvm-3.6-dev. The pinned Z3 also failed to compile with the host GCC 11 standard library.
liss.adaptation: A period-appropriate LLVM/Clang/Z3 toolchain would address the build only. A language-model translation and property correspondence are also needed for this case.
